questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.**

Trumpets are being blown by the soldiers to announce the victory.

options.text: The soldiers were blowing the trumpets to announce the victory.
The soldiers blow the trumpets to announce the victory.
The soldiers blew the trumpets to announce the victory.
The soldiers are blowing the trumpets to announce the victory.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'The soldiers are blowing the trumpets to announce the victory'.**

***__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the Passive Voice. As per the given question we have to change the sentence into Active Voice. 
 
• The given sentence is an example of 'present continuous'. 
 
• The structure of these kinds of sentences is:
 
• Subject + is/am/are + V1 + ing + Object. (Active Voice)
 
• Subject(Objective Case) + is/am/are + being+ V3 + by + Object (subjective case). (Passive Voice) 
 
• *Example:*
 
 
• *He is riding a bike. (Active Voice)*
 
• *A bike is being ridden by him. (Passive Voice)*
 
 
 
• The subject of the given sentence is 'Trumpets' and the object of the given sentence is 'the soldiers'. 
 
• The subject will be put in place of the object and the object will be put in place of the subject. 
 
• Here, 'are being blown' will be changed into 'are blowing'.

 

Correct Sentence:__ The soldiers are blowing the trumpets to announce the victory.*

questions.question:
**Direction: Select the correct active form of the given sentence.**

Many Indians have been brought back from foreign countries by the government.

options.text: The government had brought back many Indians from foreign countries.
The government is bringing back many Indians from foreign countries.
The government has brought back many Indians from foreign countries.
The government has been bringing back many Indians from foreign countries.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'****The government has brought back many Indians from foreign countries.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in Present Perfect Tense and Passive Voice.
 
• The rule for changing a Present Perfect Tense from Passive voice to Active voice:
 
 
• Interchange the object and subject with each other, i.e. object of the active sentence become the subject of the passive sentence.​
 
• Structure__: Subject + has/have + past participle (V3) + object __(Active Voice)__

 Object + has/have + been + past participle (V3) + (by + subject) __(Passive Voice)__ 
 __
 
• Example: *Disha has arranged the things. *(Active Voice)

 * The things have been arranged by Disha.** *(Passive Voice)
 
 
 
 
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is 'The government has brought back many Indians from foreign countries.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

__
 
• In Active Voice, a sentence emphasizes the subject performing an action.
 
• In Passive Voice, the sentence emphasizes the action or the object of the sentence.
 
 
• Example: *He reads a novel. *(Active Voice)

 * A novel is read by him. *(Passive Voice)*​*
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **Hinglish__** 

__
 
• दिया गया वाक्य Present Perfect Tense और Passive Voice में है।
 
• Present Perfect Tense को Passive Voice से Active voice में बदलने का नियम:
 
 
• Object और Subject को एक दूसरे के साथ बदलें, यानी Active Voice का Object, Passive Voice का Subject बन जाता है।
 
• संरचना__: Subject + has/have + past participle (V3) + object __(Active Voice)__

 Object + has/have + been + past participle (V3) + (by + subject) __(Passive Voice)__ 
 
 
• Example: *Disha has arranged the things. *(Active Voice)

 * The things have been arranged by Disha.** *(Passive Voice)

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.**

The coloured clothes should not be washed with the whites.

options.text: Do not washed the coloured clothes with the whites.
You should not wash the coloured clothes with the whites.
Do not be washing the coloured clothes with the whites.
You should not have washed the coloured clothes with the whites.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'You should not wash the coloured clothes with the whites.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is an example of Passive Voice. As per the given question we have to change it into **Active** Voice. 
 
• The process of transformation is as follows:
 
 
• Since modal verb has been used in the **passive** voice, therefore, the **active** voice will follow the given structure: 
 
 
• Passive Voice - modal verb*(should)* + be + V3
 
• Active Voice - modal verb*(should) *+ V1
 
 
 
• Here, 'should not be washed' will be changed into 'should not wash'.​
 
 

Correct Sentence:__* You should not wash the coloured clothes with the whites.*

questions.question:
**Directions: Select the correct active form of the given sentence.**

The excitement aroused by the murder was soon forgotten by people.

options.text: People are soon going to forget the excitement aroused by the murder.
People will soon forget the excitement aroused by the murder.
People have soon forgotten the excitement aroused by the murder.
People soon forgot the excitement aroused by the murder.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**People soon forgot the excitement aroused by the murder**.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/64e177b3c5c5cb81c12b3d5b5ddabaaf474cdad3d6098992ca6592786c8147d6.png] 

 
• In **Active Voice**, a sentence emphasizes the subject, performing an action.
 
• In **Passive Voice**, a sentence emphasizes the action or the object of the sentence.
 
• The **given sentence** is in the **passive voice** and '**The excitement**' is the **subject **and '**people**' is the **object.**
 
• When we convert this sentence into **active voice**, the subject '**The excitement**' of the **passive voice** becomes the** object**, the **object **'**people**' becomes the **subject**.
 
• The passive format "**was + V3 (forgotten)**" should be **converted into** the active format "**V2 (forgot)**".
 
• This is the active and passive voice **rule** for the **past simple tense**.

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

questions.question:
**Select the correct active form of the given sentence.**

So much noise ought not to be made by you and your friends

options.text: You and your friends ought to not make so much noise.
You and your friends ought not to have made so much noise.
You and your friends ought not to be making so much noise.
You and your friends ought not to make so much noise.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is- **You and your friends ought not to make so much noise.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Let's look at the structures given below in active and passive forms:

 
 
• Active- Subject + modal verb + V1 + Object.
 
• Passive- Object + modal verb + be + V3 + by + Subject.
 
 
 
• Example:
 
 
• *She might her task. (active)*
 
• *Her task might be finished by her. (passive)**​*
 
 
 
• The given sentence is an **imperative **one and in the passive voice form.
 
• Follow the active form structure for the **modals** given above:
 
 
• Exchange the places of the subject and object. (So much noise - you and your friends)
 
• Now the **modal** verb will be used followed by the **1st form of the verb.** (ought not to make)
 
 
 
• ​At last, line up the remaining part.

 

Following the active voice form, we finally get- *You and your friends ought not to make so much noise.*

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** *​​​​

 
• There is a difference between 'must' and 'have to' given below:

 
 
• Must expresses obligation or compulsion imposed by the speaker.
 
• Whereas 'have to' expresses external obligations.
 
 
 
• Example: 
 
 
• *​We must fasten our seat belts. (the speaker thinks so)*
 
• *They have to help the needy. (others think this and not the speaker)*

• *We have finalized the site for our new factory. (Active Voice) *

questions.question:
**Select the correct active form of the given sentence.**

You are advised not to travel interstate during the lockdown.

options.text: You cannot travel interstate during the lockdown.
Why don’t you travel interstate during the lockdown?
You will not travel interstate during the lockdown.
Do not travel interstate during the lockdown.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Do not travel interstate during the lockdown'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **given sentence** is in the **present tense, **and here **someone is advised **not to do something.
 
• In such a situation, **when someone is advised, requested, invited, warned, or ordered**, it is **called an imperative sentence**.
 
 
• **For example:**
 
• ***Do not go ***swimming in the cold.
 
• ***Do not watch*** t.v. shows while studying.
 
• ***Do not eat ***anything just before going to bed.
 
 
 
• If we **observe the above examples**, the **active form **of the given sentence would be:
 
 
• ***Do not travel interstate during the lockdown.***
 
 
 
• Hence, the correct answer is **option 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**Let's **understand the concept **by converting the sentences **into passive voice.**

 
• Do not go swimming in the cold. - ***You are advised not to swim during the cold.***
 
• Do not watch t.v. shows while studying. - ***You are advised not to watch t.v. shows while studying.***
 
• Do not eat anything just before going to bed. - ***You are advised not to eat anything just before going to bed.***
